claims.head: The Kraken better keep their heads up
claims.body: On physicality, Philadelphia is near the top of the league, but Seattle is one of the worst. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Flyers.

claims.head: Where the Flyers have the edge: the penalty kill
claims.body: The Flyers are around the middle of the league for the penalty kill, and the Kraken are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.

notes.text: Vince Dunn has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, up from 2% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 7 games cover only 18% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 47%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

PHI.head: Nothing to separate these two
PHI.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Philadelphia has home-ice advantage. The Flyers can tip it if their penalty kill holds up.

SEA.head: Too close to call
SEA.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Philadelphia has home-ice advantage. For the Kraken, the difference could be keeping dangerous shots away.
